title: Setup Wizard: rooms you draw are kept
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **In the Setup Wizard, press a room's name above the plan to draw it.** The rooms still to draw are buttons there; pressing one starts that room, and a line says what to do next. The room list and Start drawing under the plan work as before.

### Fixed
- **A room drawn in the Setup Wizard is saved as you finish it.** It used to wait for Save Layout, a button under the plan and off most screens: draw the rooms, press Next and Finish, and nothing had been saved, so the house ended with a floor plan and no rooms. Now each room is saved when you close its outline, and anything else unsaved (a receiver you placed) is saved when you move to another step, press Back to Setup or Exit setup. Mapping → Edit outside the wizard still waits for Save Layout, with Revert, as before.
- **A click on the plan before a room is chosen says what to do.** It used to do nothing at all.
- **A double-click that closes a room no longer leaves its last corner twice.**

### Usage report (opt-in)
- **Where setup stops, in more detail.** The report could say a house had a plan and no scale, or a plan and no rooms, but not what was tried. It now counts, as words only: on Mapping → Upload, a picture picked, Upload pressed with none, and whether the upload worked, the picture couldn't be read, was too large or failed; on the scale screen, the first end tapped, both ends down, a length typed and a Save refused; when drawing rooms, a room's name pressed above the plan, the plan clicked with no room chosen, and rooms or receivers the Setup Wizard saved for you. Never the picture, a name, a length or a place.

title: Power teams: lights found on after a restart
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **A team of lights that always have power goes on following the day after Home Assistant restarts.** When Home Assistant started with the team's lights already on, they stayed on but nothing led them until they were next switched: the team only ever answered a switch from off to on. It now takes the team up as on when its lights are first heard from, and the next minute puts the day's light back. A light that was unavailable and comes back is never read as someone's hand on it.

title: 3D look: a room's lights just outside its outline
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **A light just outside the outline of its own room is no longer drawn as an outside light.** When a room is drawn smaller than it is, its lights stand where no room is drawn, and the 3D look treated them as being on the outside of the house: a ceiling fan became a grille low on the nearest wall, and a ceiling light lost its place under the ceiling. A light that Home Assistant files under a room of its floor, that stands between half a metre and four metres outside that room's outline with a room of a higher floor over it, is now drawn as that room's light, where it was placed, under that room's ceiling. Closer than half a metre it is taken to be in or on the wall, as before (a fireplace blower stays a grille), and a light with nothing over it stays an outside light (one on a deck by the room's wall).

title: Teams of lights that always have power
body_markdown:
### New
- **A power team can have no power source (Settings → Atlas → Power teams: "None: these lights always have power").** For colour lights on their own supply, such as LED strings: they become one light that switches and changes colour together and can follow the day. One of them turned on by an automation is answered with the day's light on all of them; one turned off takes the rest with it. On and off are re-sent until each light shows it, so a light on weak Wi-Fi that drops a command still follows.

### Fixed
- **A team that follows the day puts a light back when it missed a command.** Each minute, a light that does not show what was last sent is sent it once more; the team's own re-send is never mistaken for someone choosing a colour by hand.

title: Power teams: smart bulbs on a wall dimmer, as one light that follows the day
body_markdown:
### New
- **Power teams (Settings → Atlas → Power teams).** For smart colour bulbs in sockets fed by a wall dimmer or switch (Zigbee bulbs on a Control4 dimmer, say). A team makes them one light in Home Assistant, named as you name it. Turning it on puts the power on at full, sends the bulbs their brightness and colour again and again while they start up, and says which bulb never answered. Turning it off cuts the power. The wall button still works: PadSpan sees the power come on and sets the bulbs, and a dimmer held to a level at the wall sets how bright the bulbs go while the dimmer itself is put back to full, since smart bulbs need the whole wave. None exists until you make one.
- **A team can follow the day.** Cool and bright at midday, warm at sunrise and sunset, dim and warmer through the night, set at each turn-on and moved every minute with a slow fade. Choose a colour or a brightness yourself and it stops until the team is next turned on, or until you set its effect back to "Adaptive"; the effect "Sleep" is one fixed dim, warm setting. The curve's six numbers are yours to change. The sun curve is adapted from [Adaptive Lighting](https://github.com/basnijholt/adaptive-lighting) by Bas Nijholt and contributors (Apache-2.0), with thanks; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

title: Rooms as light switches
body_markdown:
### New
- **Rooms as light switches, in the 3D look (⋯ → Lights, off unless you tick it).** At night the 3D look is as dark as the house, so a light that is off is a dark dot nobody can find or hit. With this ticked, a room's floor is the switch for its lights: tap it and they go on together, or all off if any is on (the message has Undo). Hold for the room's list, where each light has its own switch. Hold, then drag up or down, to dim the room. And a touch lights the house up as by day for 20 seconds, so everything can be seen; on a dark house the first touch only does that. Sensors, locks and doors keep their own taps. On the Atlas tab and its wall screens, per screen.

title: String lights you can see
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **String lights are easier to see in the 3D look.** A string of lights (Christmas lights along a roof edge, bulbs over a deck) was drawn to scale: bulbs 5 cm across on a thin dark wire, which is a couple of pixels when the whole house is on screen. The bulbs are now 14 cm across and the wire is thicker and lighter, so the string shows from across the house, lit or not.

title: Lights stay where you placed them; taps on sensors and locks; darker paving
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **3D look: a strip, valance, wall light or panel stays where you placed it unless a wall is within 0.75 m.** Before, each went to a wall of its room however far away, so a light placed over an island was drawn on a wall metres off and a press on what you saw missed it. Within 0.75 m it still goes onto the wall. A strip with a length takes only a wall running its way, so it is never turned. A wall light with no wall in reach is drawn at its spot at its usual height.
- **A tap on a sensor says what it reads**: "Hall temperature: 21.4 °C" at the bottom of the screen, in the flat Map and the 3D look. Before, it said only that sensors are read-only.
- **A tap on a motion sensor says its reading; a long press opens its activity.** Before, any tap opened the full-screen activity history. Both looks.
- **A tap never turns a lock.** A tap or a hold on a lock opens its card, which has Lock and Unlock. Before, a tap locked or unlocked it at once. Both looks.
- **Paving tiles are darker and textured**: a darker grey with darker joints and flecks on each tile, in the flat Map and the 3D look.

title: 3D look: easier to hit the light you mean
body_markdown:
### Changed (the 3D look on the Atlas tab and its wall screens, while "Tap a light to switch it" is on)
- **A light in reach beats a sensor.** With a light and a sensor, a lock, a leak mark or a motion marker both under the finger, the light answers. Before, the nearer of the two did, so a tap meant for a light could open the sensor beside it. With no light in reach, each of those answers as before. A tag or a person under the finger still comes first.
- **A tap that lands on nothing goes to the nearest light within 60 pixels**, if no wall or floor hides it. A fixture a few pixels across no longer has to be hit exactly. Fans are left out.
- **What you press says its name beside your finger** while you hold it. Sliding away before lifting still cancels, as before.
- **A light switched by a tap says so, with Undo**: "Kitchen East off · Undo" for a few seconds. A wrong light costs one more tap.
Not changed: what a tap does on each kind of device (a motion sensor's activity, a lock's switch) stays the same as on the flat Map.

title: 3D look: bigger fixtures, and buttons at the placed spot
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Round light fixtures are drawn bigger in the 3D look.** A pot light was drawn its real 15 cm and a plain light as a 7 cm ball: a few pixels from across a room. A pot, a dome and a single-bulb light are now never drawn smaller than 26 cm across (at most three times their size). Strips, tubes, panels and chandeliers keep their size.
- **A light that is off is solid and lighter.** It was half see-through and leaned to the theme's dark colour, so it all but vanished at night.
- **⋯ → "Lights as buttons": a button now sits at the spot the light was placed on the map**, with its line to the nearest part of the fixture as drawn. It sat under the middle of what was drawn, which for a ring of pots round a room is nowhere near any of them, and for a strip drawn on a wall can be metres from its spot.

title: Lights as buttons: each button under its light
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **⋯ → "Lights as buttons": a light's button now sits on the floor straight under the light, with a dotted line up to the light itself and a dot on it.** In 0.38.237 the button sat on the fixture. With the ceiling cut away, a ceiling light's button then hung in the air and showed over another room, so it was not clear where the light was. On the floor, a button is in its room and at its spot, and the line shows which fixture it switches. A button for several lights has a line to each of them.

title: Move a light in the 3D editor
body_markdown:
### Added
- **Mapping → Atlas builder → 3D look → Edit → Heights → "Move it".** A light, a sensor or a readout could have its height and its kind ("What is this?") set in the 3D look, but its place only on the flat map. Now: tap the device, press **Move it**, then tap its new place on the same floor.
  - The move is written to the device's place on the map at once. It is not part of the editor's Save, Undo or Discard; **Put it back** undoes the last move.
  - Its height and everything else about it stay as they are.
  - A tap on another floor is refused, with where a device changes floor (the flat map).
- **The Heights sheet says when a light is drawn away from where it is placed.** A strip, a sconce and a few other kinds are drawn on the nearest wall or round their room; when that is more than half a metre from the spot, the sheet says how far, and that "What is this?" changes it.

title: Lights as buttons in the 3D look
body_markdown:
### Added
- **⋯ → "Lights as buttons" (the 3D look on the Atlas tab and its wall screens; off until you tick it).** In the 3D look a light that is off is drawn its real size, which from across a room is a few pixels, and a tap meant for it could land on the sensor beside it. With this ticked:
  - **Every light on the floors showing is a round button of one size**, standing on the light and drawn over the walls: gold when it is on, dark when it is off. The button is what a tap lands on, so what you see is what you hit. A hold still opens the light's controls, and a hold then a drag still dims it.
  - **Buttons that would overlap become one, with their count.** A tap on it lists those lights, each with its own switch, with "All on" and "All off".
  - **A tap anywhere else in a room opens that room's sheet**: its lights and other devices, with all lights on or off. A sensor, a temperature chip or a lock under the finger opens its room too, instead of answering the tap itself; holding it still opens it. While a class chip (Motion, Temps, …) is picked, that class answers taps as before.
  - A light on a floor hidden under another floor has no button and takes no tap.
  - Double-tap to fly to a room is not available while this is ticked: the first tap opens the room's sheet.
- Each screen keeps its own tick, as for the rest of the ⋯ list. Nothing changes on a screen that leaves it unticked.
- The opt-in usage report counts the tick, and taps on a button, on a button for several lights and on a room. Counts only, never a name.

title: Taps on lights in the 3D look; Small fixes after the set-up round
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **A tap on something the device filter has dimmed now says why nothing happened.** With one of the ☰ chips picked (Lights, Motion, Temps and so on), everything else is dimmed and takes no taps. In the Atlas's 3D look that was silent: a wall left on Motion looked as if its lights were broken. A tap on a dimmed device now shows "Only Motion takes taps now: the rest is dimmed." with a **Show all** button that puts the filter back to All.
- **A tap with a finger switches the light in the 3D look even if the finger rolls a little.** If it moved more than 8 pixels (about 3 mm on a wall screen) the tap was treated as the start of a turn of the house and did nothing. A finger may now move up to 16 pixels and still count as a tap. A mouse is unchanged, and so is the flat Map.
- **On a phone, the "Save the scale" bar no longer lies over the plan.** On the one-length scale screen the bar was held at the bottom of the screen, over the lower part of the picture where the two ends are tapped. On a narrow screen it now comes after the length, as an ordinary row.
- **The Rooms page's "Put it on the map" shows that it is working.** The button reads "Putting it on the map…" and can't be pressed twice while it writes.
- **The Atlas header's tip follows ⋯ "Tap a light to switch it" at once.** It used to keep the old words until the page was next drawn.
- **Escape closes a tag's, person's or receiver's card in the 3D look**, as ✕ does.
- **The Atlas builder's guide opens by itself once.** If it was left open and never closed, it came back on every visit. "Guide me" still opens it.
- **Wording.** The guided tour's Overview picture and its troubleshooting line say "Receivers", as the screens do. A calibration point heard by one receiver reads "(1 receiver)".
